summary: Practise surveillance planning, source assessment and evidence records. Explore the five-day course and its casework deliverables.
lede: Surveillance, profiling, and evidence documentation combine structured observation and source assessment to build traceable case records. For investigators, security analysts, and case supervisors, the course addresses turning fragmented observations and digital material into clear case files. Participants practise planning surveillance, assessing sources and links, and documenting digital evidence and case chronologies while distinguishing verified facts from inferences and unresolved leads.
audienceIntro: This intermediate course suits professionals who plan or review surveillance activity, assess investigative information, or maintain evidence records. It is designed for roles that need to turn fragmented observations and digital material into clear, traceable case files.
modules: Chain of Custody and Case Files
prerequisites: Prior work in investigations, security, compliance, fraud, or evidence handling is recommended. No programming is required; exercises use provided case scenarios and documentation templates rather than specialist forensic software.
